transcript:
Header: 2025-10-22 14:00 PT | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Anna Park (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Morris (Redwood SE), Tom Wu (Redwood CSM) -- Emily Zhang (Pegasus CTO), Mike Lopez (Pegasus Head of ML), Sara Nguyen (Pegasus Platform), Daniel Reed (Product)

Summary (auto): POC to validate cost & latency tradeoffs for Pegasus' QA product. Run benchmarks and deliver cost model.

[00:00] Anna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — im Anna, i'll be your AE, Raj is our SE, Leah on bench infra. um, Emily, do you want to kick off with goals?
[00:12] Emily Zhang: Sure thanks. We're trying to scope a 3-week POC to validate two things: one, that we can hit p95 latencies under ~800ms for single-turn QA at our expected QPS; and two, that the per-token cost for production will be under our budget threshold — roughly $0.60 per 1k responses, which is a messy way to say we need a predictable per-token number.
[00:34] Raj Patel: ok got it. when you say QPS, what's your normal and peak?
[00:38] Mike Lopez: Normal is about 15 qps, peak bursts to around 75 for campaign spikes. Average prompt length is ~180 tokens in, about 120 tokens out. we do a lot of context windows with user history, so sometimes 2-3k context.
[00:55] Raj Patel: that context size matters a lot for cost and latency. the KV cache and batching behavior will change unit economics. If you can trim long histories with relevant prefix caching we can save tokens.
[01:08] Sara Nguyen: quick Q on network — for Dedicated POC do you support VPC peering and private endpoints? we have strict egress policy.
[01:15] Leah Morris: yes we do, Dedicated supports VPC peering or private endpoints, we can provide config snippets. for hosted we have region controls and encryption at rest + in transit, SOC2 compliance.
[01:26] Daniel Reed: okay on success criteria — besides p95 < 800ms what about quality/regression? we need to ensure model responses don't degrade compared to current baseline.
[01:34] Anna Park: right, so we'll include a small eval set from your 500 prompts to check for semantic regression; we propose regression threshold of <5% drop in our eval metric (F1 / exact match depends on your metric).
[01:46] Emily Zhang: that sounds reasonable. can you give rough per-token pricing guidance now?
[01:50] Raj Patel: high-level: hosted API per-token is higher but you get easy scaling and no infra ops. Dedicated has a lower per-token compute delta if you saturate GPUs, but you pay reserved capacity. For a workload like yours, with 15 qps baseline and 75 burst, we often see the break-even at around 100M-200M tokens/month depending on batching. For rough numbers: hosted might be ~$0.020 - $0.045 per 1k input tokens depending on model, dedicated effective compute cost could drop that by 30-50% if you use batching and KV cache aggressively. these are ballpark — we'll model exact numbers after benchmark.
[02:28] Mike Lopez: can you explain how batching influences latency vs cost?
[02:32] Raj Patel: sure. batching packs multiple requests into one GPU step; that amortizes the token compute cost but increases tail latency because requests wait in the batch window. we can tune batch size and max wait (e.g., 5-30ms) to balance p95 latency vs throughput. also continuous batching with smaller windows sometimes gives best of both worlds.
[02:51] Leah Morris: and caching — prefix/KV cache means if your prompts reuse earlier context like user history, those cached KV entries reduce work for subsequent tokens; this reduces per-token compute and latency. quantization helps too (int8/4) for cost but might slightly affect quality.
[03:08] Emily Zhang: for the benchmark what configs do you recommend we run?
[03:12] Raj Patel: we propose three configs: (A) Hosted standard model (lowest friction), (B) Dedicated reserved with batching optimized and int8 quantization, (C) Dedicated with KV cache enabled and conservative batching. For each run: 1k representative prompts (you provide 500-1k), run at realistic QPS patterns including bursts, capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, and cost estimate per million tokens.
[03:40] Mike Lopez: will you simulate user-history sizes? i.e., some requests with 3k context?
[03:45] Raj Patel: yes we will include scenarios: short (300 tokens), medium (1k tokens), long (2-3k tokens) to show sensitivity.
[03:53] Emily Zhang: timeline? we need results before month end ideally.
[03:56] Anna Park: proposed timeline: Pegasus provides prompt set + QPS profile by Fri 10/24; Redwood runs benchmarks 10/25-10/29; review meeting week of 11/03 to go over results and cost model, then decide on POC provisioning. so about 1-2 weeks of setup + 1 week of running tests.
[04:15] Daniel Reed: what's included in the cost model deliverable?
[04:18] Anna Park: we'll produce a spreadsheet with per-config per-token compute cost, estimated monthly cost at your projected QPS, sensitivity to batching windows, expected latency percentiles, and recommended config (hosted vs dedicated) with an estimate of break-even. we'll also include runbook for switching to Dedicated and expected commit sizes to reach target per-token.
[04:39] Mike Lopez: any caveats around SOC2 or data residency?
[04:42] Tom Wu: we are SOC2 Type II compliant, support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments, and Dedicated/Private options can be deployed in customer VPC/region for residency. we'll share our security docs and ATO checklist.
[04:58] Emily Zhang: ok budget: we can commit to a POC budget of $25k for the pilot. is that sufficient to run the dedicated reserved if needed?
[05:06] Anna Park: for a short POC, hosted runs and a small Dedicated trial (spot-like or short reserved) are possible within that budget, but sustained Dedicated for production needs larger commits. We'll model costs so you see what is doable within $25k.
[05:24] Mike Lopez: curious specifics: you mentioned 30-50% cost reduction on Dedicated — is that mostly from batching or from kernel/hardware selection?
[05:29] Raj Patel: it's a combo — kernel selection and optimized runtimes on GPUs, plus bigger batching windows and caching. also multi-instance packing for high throughput can reduce idle GPU cycles. quantization reduces memory bandwidth and sometimes improves throughput. we'll quantify each effect in the benchmark report.
[05:52] Sara Nguyen: network latency will matter; our infra sits in us-east-1; can you run Dedicated in us-east-1 and show network p95?
[05:59] Leah Morris: yes, we'll provision test instances in us-east-1 for parity. we'll measure end-to-end latency including network.
[06:07] Daniel Reed: what success criteria should we sign off on after the benchmark?
[06:10] Anna Park: propose success criteria for the POC: 1) p95 latency under 800ms for medium prompts (1k tokens) during baseline QPS; 2) per-token cost estimate that projects to <=$X (we left placeholder, need your budget target) or shows clear path to meet your $/1k response goal; 3) regression <5% on provided eval set; 4) ops checklist satisfied (VPC, SSO, encryption).
[06:36] Emily Zhang: our $/1k response target was roughly $0.60 — can you map that to tokens?
[06:41] Raj Patel: if your average request consumes 300 in + 120 out = 420 tokens, $0.60 per 1k responses is a weird unit — better to think $ per million tokens. We'll translate: $0.60 per 1k responses with avg 420 tokens ~= $1.43 per 1k tokens, which is high; I think you might mean $0.60 per 1k tokens? let's confirm offline.
[07:02] Mike Lopez: yeah that's likely my bad. we'll clarify.
[07:06] Anna Park: no worries — we'll convert all to $/M tokens in the spreadsheet and show mapping to per-response costs given your token distributions.
[07:14] Leah Morris: for the benchmark we'll instrument token accounting, and show how batching window and KV cache change tokens billed vs tokens saved. note: some caching reduces compute but you still bill tokens depending on policy — we'll call out billing assumptions.
[07:30] Emily Zhang: how do you handle model rollbacks if quality drops mid POC?
[07:34] Raj Patel: we have rollout policies with automatic fallback to previous model variants and can do canary tests. Redwood Console has tracing so we can correlate regressions to prompts and roll back quickly.
[07:46] Daniel Reed: ok any blockers from our side?
[07:48] Sara Nguyen: i'll need a security contact to review SOC2 and VPC peering docs, and i'll need credentialed test account for Dedicated if we go that route.
[07:57] Anna Park: Tom will send security pack and create a short checklist; Leah will include Dedicated quickstart.
[08:04] Emily Zhang: track of deliverables?
[08:06] Tom Wu: I'll open a shared folder and invite Pegasus; Anna will post the pricing spreadsheet there.
[08:14] Anna Park: recap: Pegasus provides prompt set + QPS profile by 10/24; Redwood runs bench 10/25-10/29; Raj shares results and cost model by 10/29; meet wk of 11/03 to review; decision on POC provisioning after that.
[08:30] Emily Zhang: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:34] Anna Park: thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links. bye.
